rows.evidence: Image is the e-rara generated cover sheet, not the title page; it and the catalogue give 'Ornithologiae libri tres ... Londini, 1676'. The English title page is the same title word for word ('The Ornithology of Francis Willughby of Middleton in the County of Warwick Esq ... In Three Books') and says 'Translated into English, and enlarged with many Additions' by John Ray, 1678.

Unrelated works: ours is the humanist Agostino Dati's Elegantiae with Badius Ascensius's and others' treatises on letter-writing and orthography; the English is 'The Rule of the great S. Augustin expounded by ... Hugh of S. Victor', i.e. the monastic rule of St Augustine of Hippo via a French version. Only the name Augustinus is shared (known: Augustinus Dathus of Siena is not Augustine of Hippo).

Our title page reads 'IVVENALIS. PERSIVS.' (the satires of Juvenal and Persius); the English is 'Poems, with The tenth Satyre of Iuvenal Englished. By Henry Vaughan', 1646. The English volume is mostly Vaughan's own original poems and translates only ONE of Juvenal's sixteen satires (Satire 10) and nothing of Persius, so it is a small part of our book, not a substantial one.

Our book per catalogue is Virgil's complete works with commentaries ('Bucolicorum eclogae X, Georgicorum libri IIII, Aeneidos libri XII ... Servii ... commentarii'); the English (Brinsley, 1620) is 'Virgils Eclogues, with his booke De apibus ... Translated Gramatically', i.e. the Eclogues and Georgics book 4 only. The originals of the English text are two of the works inside our collected Virgil.

Our book per catalogue is Malebranche's 'Réponse à une dissertation de Mr. Arnauld', a polemical reply about an Eclaircissement of the Traité de la nature et de la grace; the English title page lists 'Treatise concerning the Search after Truth', 'Treatise of Nature and Grace', 'Answer to the Animadversions upon the First Volume' and 'Defence against the Accusations of Monsieur De la Ville' and nam

Ours is Ovid's Metamorphoses with Sabinus's interpretation; the English is 'The fable of Ouid treting of Narcissus, translated out of Latin into Englysh Mytre, with a moral ther vnto', 1560. It translates ONE episode only (known: Narcissus, Metamorphoses book 3) and adds a long original English verse moral, so it is a small excerpt of our work, not a substantial part; the moral is not Sabinus's.
